laplace_resolvent_proof_steps.step_2_normal_convergence_of_partial_fra: For Re(w) > L/2, int_0^infty e^{-wt} tau^{t(rho - 1/2)} dt = 1 / (w - L(rho - 1/2)). Since sum_rho m_rho |a_rho| < infty, the partial-fraction series R_tau(w) := sum_rho m_rho a_rho / (w - L(rho - 1/2)) converges normally on every compact subset of C \ {L(rho - 1/2)} and coincides with the Laplace transform L[C_tau(-t)](w) = int_0^infty e^{-wt} C_tau(-t) dt on Re(w) > L/2.
laplace_resolvent_proof_steps.step_3_right_half_plane_holomorphy_from_: Under |C_tau(-t)| <= C_tau(0) for all t >= 0, the Laplace integral L[C_tau(-t)](w) converges absolutely and defines a holomorphic function on the entire open right half-plane Re(w) > 0, with |L[C_tau(-t)](w)| <= C_tau(0) / Re(w).
laplace_resolvent_proof_steps.step_4_nonvanishing_simple_pole_residue: If zeta(s) had a zero rho_0 = 1/2 + delta_0 + i*gamma_0 with 0 < delta_0 < 1/2, then w_0 := L(rho_0 - 1/2) = L*delta_0 + i*L*gamma_0 lies in Re(w) = L*delta_0 > 0. Because the map rho |-> w_rho = L(rho - 1/2) is injective on C, no other distinct zero rho != rho_0 shares the pole point w_0; the residue of R_tau(w) at w = w_0 is m_{rho_0} a_{rho_0} = m_{rho_0} F_tau(rho_0) conj(F_tau(1 - conj(rho_0))) != 0 (since m_{rho_0} >= 1 and F_tau(s) != 0 on 0 < Re(s) < 1), contradicting holomorphy on Re(w) > 0.
laplace_resolvent_proof_steps.step_5_functional_equation_reflection: If rho_0 = 1/2 + delta_0 + i*gamma_0 had -1/2 < delta_0 < 0, the functional equation xi(1 - s) = xi(s) supplies the reflected zero rho_0' = 1 - conj(rho_0) = 1/2 - delta_0 + i*gamma_0 with Re(rho_0' - 1/2) = -delta_0 > 0, reducing to Step 4.
laplace_resolvent_proof_steps.step_6_converse_under_rh: Under RH, every nontrivial zero has rho = 1/2 + i*gamma_rho, so 1 - conj(rho) = rho, a_rho = |F_tau(1/2 + i*gamma_rho)|^2 > 0, and C_tau(0) = sum_rho m_rho |F_tau(rho)|^2 > 0. For every real K, |C_tau(K)| = |sum_rho m_rho |F_tau(rho)|^2 tau^{-i K gamma_rho L}| <= sum_rho m_rho |F_tau(rho)|^2 = C_tau(0).

For Re(z) > 1/2 (sigma := Re(z)+1/2 > 1), sum_{n>=2} Lambda(n) n^{-sigma} = -zeta'(sigma)/zeta(sigma) < infty and sum_{k>=2} (log k) k^{-sigma} = -zeta'(sigma) < infty. Hence on 1/2 < Re(z) < 5/2, the double integral-sums for M_X[W](z) and M_X[W_log](z) converge absolutely and Fubini-Tonelli interchange yields M_X[W](z) = -H_0(z) zeta'(z+1/2)/zeta(z+1/2) and M_X[W_log](z) = -H_0(z) zeta'(z+1/2).

defect_3a_spectral_aggregation_and_synth.meromorphic_continuation_statement: By meromorphic continuation from 1/2 < Re(z) < 5/2 to the open kernel strip |Re(z)| < 5/2 (and C), harmonic divisor aggregation multiplies M_X[W](z) by zeta(z + 1/2), cancelling the poles of -zeta'(z+1/2)/zeta(z+1/2) at all actual nontrivial zeros rho = 1/2 + z_rho of zeta(s) IRRESPECTIVE of their real parts, while the triple zero H_0(1/2) = H_0'(1/2) = H_0''(1/2) = 0 cancels the double pole of -zeta'(z+1/2) at z = 1/2. Thus M_X[W_log](z) = -H_0(z) zeta'(z+1/2) extends HOLOMORPHICALLY to the open kernel strip |Re(z)| < 5/2, and MEROMORPHICALLY (NOT entire) to C, where H_0(z) = F_tau(1/2+z)F_tau(1/2-z) has simple poles at z = +/-(2k + 1/2) (k >= 1) from the Gamma poles of F_tau(s) at s = -2k <= -2 (in particular a simple pole at z = 5/2 with residue Res_{z=5/2}[-H_0(z)zeta'(z+1/2)] = (81/64)(-zeta'(3)) = +0.2507535262 != 0). Conversely, Moebius inversion W(X) = sum_{m>=1} (mu(m)/sqrt(m)) W_log(X/m) multiplies M_X[W_log](z) by sum_{m>=1} mu(m) m^{-(z+1/2)} = 1/zeta(z+1/2) on Re(z) > 1/2 and by meromorphic continuation restores the denominator zeta(z + 1/2).

synthetic_quartet_convergence_and_regula.ordinary_dirichlet_series_divergence: For 0 < Re(rho_0) < 1, the ordinary Dirichlet series sum_{m=1}^infty m^{-rho_0} diverges (its partial sums oscillate with amplitude O(M^{1 - Re(rho_0)}) / |1 - rho_0|); a numerical evaluation of zeta(rho_0) does NOT make the unsubtracted series converge on an isolated mode X^{rho_0 - 1/2}.
synthetic_quartet_convergence_and_regula.actual_W_vs_isolated_mode_explanation: On the actual profile W(X), the unsubtracted sum sum_{m=1}^infty m^{-1/2} W(X/m) converges absolutely because W(u) = O(u^{5/2}) as u -> 0^+ (since all poles in |Re(z)| < 5/2 including s = 1 and all nontrivial zeros cancel in the contour shift to Re(z) -> -5/2^+, where the simple pole of H_0(z) at z = -5/2 generates the leading small-scale term O(u^{5/2})). An isolated synthetic mode X^{rho_0 - 1/2} has not been combined with a pole-cancelling completion at small scales, so divisor aggregation on the isolated mode requires the Euler-Maclaurin pole-subtracted regularization lim_{M->infty} (sum_{m=1}^M m^{-rho_0} - M^{1-rho_0}/(1-rho_0) - (1/2) M^{-rho_0}) = zeta(rho_0).

small_scale_decay_lemma.proof: By the exact rational Bernstein envelope |h_0(alpha)| <= (92193/32768)(alpha + alpha^{-1})^{-5/2} <= (92193/32768) alpha^{-5/2} applied at alpha = k/u, each term satisfies |(log k / sqrt(k)) h_0(k/u)| <= (92193/32768) u^{5/2} (log k) k^{-3}. Summing over k >= 2 yields |W_log(u)| <= (92193/32768)(-zeta'(3)) u^{5/2} = O(u^{5/2}). Furthermore, for 0 < u <= 2/9, k/u >= 9 for all k >= 2, so h_0(k/u) in [-(81/64)(u/k)^{5/2}, 0) and -(81/64)(-zeta'(3)) u^{5/2} <= W_log(u) < 0.

mixed_grade_polarization_identity.retains_B_transfer_and_both_scale_direct: B_known(K, L) = W_arch(h_{K-L}) - W(tau^{-|K-L|}) - W_log(tau^{|K-L|}) retains B_transfer(T_K psi_tau, T_L psi_tau) inside W_arch(h_{K-L}) = <A_tau^B T_K psi_tau, A_tau^B T_L psi_tau> - c_tau^B h_0(tau^{|K-L|}) + B_transfer(T_K psi_tau, T_L psi_tau) and retains both scale directions tau^{|K-L|} (in W_log(tau^{|K-L|}) + R_mu(tau^{|K-L|})) and tau^{-|K-L|} (in W(tau^{-|K-L|})).
mixed_grade_polarization_identity.equivalence_theorem: For all K, L in A_R, |C_tau(K - L) + R_mu(tau^{|K-L|})| = |Q_tau(T_K psi_tau, T_L psi_tau) + R_mu(tau^{|K-L|})| = |B_known(K, L)| <= 7.07942813 < 9.27739781 < 9.4468. Consequently, uniform boundedness of the mixed-grade pairings sup_{K,L in A_R} |Q_tau(T_K psi_tau, T_L psi_tau)| = sup_{K in A_R} |C_tau(K)| < infty is unconditionally equivalent to uniform boundedness sup_{X >= 1} |R_mu(X)| < infty (and sup_{X >= 1} |W(X)| < infty), without dividing by ||f_-^{(K)}||_{L^2}^2. Coercive relative semiboundedness on f_pm^{(K)} is treated separately as a conditional one-way sufficient hypothesis (`coercive_norm_shift_semiboundedness_implies_correlation_bound`).

simultaneous_grade_covariance_and_counte.obstruction_conclusion: Simultaneous-grade shift covariance, Hermitian symmetry, diagonal positivity K(K, K) = C_tau(0) > 0, and real-analytic continuity on R x R hold identically for K_model(K, L), yet |K_model(K, L)| grows as O(tau^{delta_0 |K - L|}) -> infty. mertens_stieltjes_representation_of_R_mu.unconditional_mertens_bound_obstruction: Inserting the strongest known unconditional zero-free-region Mertens bounds |M(y)| <= C_mu y exp(-c_mu sqrt(log y)) (Schoenfeld 1969; El Marraki 1995; Titchmarsh 1986, Section 14.26) into R_mu(X) = X^{-1/2} int_0^{X/2} M_{>=2}(X/u) phi_log'(u) du yields only an unsigned upper bound |R_mu(X)| <= X^{1/2} int_0^{X/2} |M_{>=2}(X/u)/(X/u)| u^{-1} |phi_log'(u)| du = O(X^{1/2} exp(-c_mu' sqrt(log X))) -> +infty as X -> infty, because the X^{-1/2} prefactor cancels only half a power of y = X/u ~ X. This growing upper bound shows that an unsigned point-wise Mertens bound is insufficient to prove O(1) boundedness (it does NOT prove that the signed integral R_mu(X) itself diverges). Achieving O(1) boundedness requires exploiting signed cancellation of M_{>=2}(X/u) against the smooth derivative kernel phi_log'(u) (or an arithmetic-Fourier positivity identity on S_tau).
